<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Extended related work</h2>

<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reference Resets</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We here provide an overview of alternative explanations for reference-resets and related methods.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Noukhovitch et al. (2023)</a></cite> proposed Elastic Resets, a method which maintains an exponential moving average of the weights <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> during the updates. After each <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> steps, the current policy parameters are replaced with the EMA weights <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\phi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\phi}</annotation></semantics></math> and the EMA weights are reinitialized to the initial policy <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Next, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorbatovski et al., 2025</a>)</cite> proposed Trust-Region Direct Preference Optimization (TR-DPO), which proposes a method very similar to reference resets, applied to DPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rafailov et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
Similar to Reference Resets, the reference policy is set to the current policy after each <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> updates.
While DPO is meant to increase the probability of preferred responses <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(a_{\mathrm{w}}|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(a_{\mathrm{w}}|s)</annotation></semantics></math> while decreasing the probability of un-preferred responses <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(a_{\mathrm{l}}|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(a_{\mathrm{l}}|s)</annotation></semantics></math>, in practice it often decreases both <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(a_{\mathrm{w}}|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>w</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(a_{\mathrm{w}}|s)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(a_{\mathrm{l}}|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(a_{\mathrm{l}}|s)</annotation></semantics></math>, degrading performance.
This issue is known as likelihood displacement <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Razin et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gorbatovski et al. (2025)</a></cite> motivate the mechanism of TR-DPO by preventing likelihood displacement, however likelihood displacement does not occur in on-policy alignment methods such as GRPO, which we investigate in this work.
This mechanism can thus not explain why Reference Resets improve over standard GRPO.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025a)</a></cite> motivate the need for Reference Resets in reasoning training due to the magnitude of the KL penalty overwhelming the magnitude of the reward after a certain number of training steps.
However, if this was the reason, we could simply use a smaller KL penalty <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> from the beginning, which we show in <a href="#A5.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Appendix E Reference Resets in RLHF ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 15</span></a> does not work.
Another reasonable approach following the reasoning of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> would be to simply decrease <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> when the reward stagnates, but we also show in the experiments (<a href="#A4.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ D.4 KL penalty schedule ‣ Appendix D Additional Experiments ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref ltx_refmacro_autoref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure 14</span></a>) that this does not work as well as Reference Resets.
Instead, we provide a theoretical analysis explaining its success and provide experiments validating it specifically in the RLHF setting.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ackermann et al. (2025)</a></cite> contemporarily to <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2025a)</a></cite> proposed reference resets as an ablation called “PPO + New KL”.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Replacing the KL penalty in Post-training</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The most common way to prevent reward hacking with proxy rewards is a KL penalty, introduced in RLHF by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stiennon et al. (2020)</a></cite> and RLVR by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Havrilla et al. (2024)</a></cite>.
Some recent reports about large model training, for example GLM4.5 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">GLM-4.5 Team et al., 2025</a>)</cite> and Olmo3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Olmo Team et al., 2025</a>)</cite> remove the KL penalty, while others such as Kimi K2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kimi Team et al., 2025</a>)</cite> still use it.
Our experiments show that both in RLHF and math experiments using gradient regularization performs better than either the KL penalty or removing the KL penalty.
Direct alignment methods such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rafailov et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ethayarajh et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, do not use an explicit KL penalty during training, however they indirectly optimize the KL-constrained RL objective.
Instead of just a KL penalty <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ouyang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> uses <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">PPO-ptx</span> which adds an additional behavior cloning term to the loss, on data sampled from a pretraining dataset, to prevent regressions on standard NLP benchmarks during RLHF training.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gradient Regularization</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karakida et al., 2023</a>)</cite> performs experiments with convolutional neural networks, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> further apply GR to vision transformer models.
Sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Foret et al., 2021</a>)</cite> has been shown to correspond to gradient regularization with a specific choice of hyper-parameters <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karakida et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bahri et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2022</a>)</cite> apply SAM to transformer pre-training in order to improve generalization.
SAM has also been used in RL, particularly by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. (2023)</a></cite> to improve sample efficiency when training a policy for Atari games, and by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee and Yoon, 2025</a>)</cite> to obtain robust policies in continuous control tasks.
Our theoretical analysis in part uses the argument provided <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee and Yoon, 2025</a>)</cite>, relating parameter flatness to action robustness.
Our work is, to our knowledge, the first one to investigate the relation of GR to the accuracy of proxy rewards, as well as the first work to use GR in RLHF/RLVR post-training of LMs.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Proof(s)</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our argument can be summarized as follows:
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee and Yoon (2025)</a></cite> showed that flatness in parameter space is related to flatness in action space, we slightly extend the argument to a maximum error of <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> in Proposition <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem5" title="Proposition B.5 ( ℰ-𝐿̂ flat return implies 𝐷-𝐿̂ robust policy, slightly modified from ( ) ). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>.
In our case this controls the expected proxy reward inside, when assuming a Gaussian policy with fixed covariance and full row-rank Jacobian (Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption B.2 (Gaussian policy with fixed covariance and full row-rank Jacobian). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>).
Under the assumption of <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> smoothness of the expected proxy reward (Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption B.3 (Action-smooth proxy reward). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>), this provides a bound on the gradient norm of the expected proxy reward (Lemma <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem6" title="Lemma B.6 (Flatness and 𝛽-smoothness imply bounded gradient). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a>).
We then relate the gradient norm of the expected proxy reward to the point-wise norm of the action-gradient in Lemma <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem7" title="Lemma B.7 (Pointwise action-gradient is controlled by Gaussian-smoothing). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.7</span></a>.
Then, as in an area with a bounded gradient norm Lipschitz continuity is guaranteed, in Lemma <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem8" title="Lemma B.8 (Pairwise robustness is bounded by local smoothness). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.8</span></a> we show that overly sharp action pairs can only occur if at least one of the actions is outside of a certain radius from the maximum.
Putting it all together yields Proposition <a href="#S3.Ex2" title="Proposition 3.3 ( ℰ-𝐿̂ flat reward implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌) robust policy). ‣ Flat Maxima in Parameter Space imply Robust Maxima in Action Space ‣ 3.2 Gradient Regularization Improves Proxy Reward Accuracy ‣ 3 Accurate Proxy Rewards via Gradient Regularization ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>.
Finally, we show that, under a Lipschitz continuous true reward (Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem4" title="Assumption B.4 (Lipschitz-continuous true reward). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>), sharp minima incur an excess BT error.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Flatness in Parameter Space implies <math id="A2.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\delta,K,\rho)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\delta,K,\rho)</annotation></semantics></math>-pairwise robustness</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We will first show that a <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> flat reward implies a <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robust policy, closely based on the proof proposed by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee and Yoon (2025)</a></cite>.
We also need to define a <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> action robust policy:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition B.1</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> action robust policy, slightly modified from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee and Yoon (2025)</a></cite>)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a reward function <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> and policy <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}(a|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}(a|s)</annotation></semantics></math>, parameterized by <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, a maximum <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>-<math id="A2.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> action robust if the following holds:</p>
<table id="A2.E11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="A2.E11X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.E11X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{For all }\delta\in\mathbb{R}^{|A|}\text{ s.t. }\|\delta\|\leq D:\quad\quad\quad\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi_{\phi^{*}}}\left[\widetilde{R}(s,a)\right]-\mathbb{E}_{a\sim\pi_{\phi^{*}}}\left[\widetilde{R}(s,a+\delta)\right]\leq\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We will also need the following assumptions during this section:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption B.2</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Gaussian policy with fixed covariance and full row-rank Jacobian)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\pi_{\phi^{*}}(\cdot\mid s)=\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\phi^{*}}(s),\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi^{*}}(\cdot\mid s)=\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\phi^{*}}(s),\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> with a fixed positive definite covariance <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. The Jacobian matrix <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{J}(\phi^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔍</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{J}(\phi^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> of the mean action <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\phi}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\phi}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> w.r.t. <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, evaluated at <math id="A2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, has full row rank.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption B.3</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Action-smooth proxy reward)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For all <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, the PR <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{R}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{R}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smooth in <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,
<math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla_{a}\widetilde{R}(s,a_{1})-\nabla_{a}\widetilde{R}(s,a_{2})\|\leq\beta\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla_{a}\widetilde{R}(s,a_{1})-\nabla_{a}\widetilde{R}(s,a_{2})\|\leq\beta\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1},a_{2}\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1},a_{2}\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_assumption">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Assumption B.4</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Lipschitz-continuous true reward)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For all <math id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math>, the true reward <math id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{*}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{*}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> is Lipschitz in <math id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|R^{*}(s,a_{1})-R^{*}(s,a_{2})|\leq L\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|R^{*}(s,a_{1})-R^{*}(s,a_{2})|\leq L\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1},a_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1},a_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We now can show that an <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> flat return implies <math id="A2.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robust policy:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.5</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>( <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> flat return implies <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robust policy, slightly modified from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee and Yoon (2025)</a></cite>)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> is an <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> flat return maximum of a policy under assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption B.2 (Gaussian policy with fixed covariance and full row-rank Jacobian). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>, then the policy <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{*}-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{*}-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robust, where:</span></p>
<table id="A2.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{*}\leq\bigl\lVert\mathfrak{J}(\phi^{*})\bigr\rVert\,\mathcal{E}+\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{E}^{2})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>≤</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔍</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{*}\leq\bigl\lVert\mathfrak{J}(\phi^{*})\bigr\rVert\,\mathcal{E}+\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{E}^{2}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">and</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{J}(\phi^{*}):=\nabla_{\phi}\,\mu_{\phi}(s)\bigm|_{\phi=\phi^{*}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔍</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><msub><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" stretchy="true">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{J}(\phi^{*}):=\nabla_{\phi}\,\mu_{\phi}(s)\bigm|_{\phi=\phi^{*}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is the Jacobian matrix of the mean action <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\phi}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\phi}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>, evaluated at <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Assume a Gaussian policy with fixed covariance <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, such that <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\phi}(a|s)=\mathcal{N}(a;\mu_{\phi}(s),\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\phi}(a|s)=\mathcal{N}(a;\mu_{\phi}(s),\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\phi}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\phi}(s)</annotation></semantics></math> is the mean of the Gaussian we are training.
A Taylor expansion yields
<math id="A2.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{\phi+\epsilon}(s)=\mu_{\phi}(s)+J(\phi)\epsilon+O(||\epsilon||^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{\phi+\epsilon}(s)=\mu_{\phi}(s)+J(\phi)\epsilon+O(||\epsilon||^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define the change in policy for a given state <math id="A2.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> due to the perturbation <math id="A2.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> as</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">Thus a <math id="A2.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> flat reward maximum implies a <math id="A2.SS1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{*}-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{*}-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robust policy with <math id="A2.SS1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{*}\leq||J(\phi^{*})||\mathcal{E}+\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{E}^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>D</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{*}\leq||J(\phi^{*})||\mathcal{E}+\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{E}^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">As we want to show an excess BT loss based on a Lipschitz-continuity assumption, which is defined over action pairs, we need to relate <math id="A2.SS1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robustness to <math id="A2.SS1.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(S_{K,\delta}|\pi_{\phi})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(S_{K,\delta}|\pi_{\phi})</annotation></semantics></math>.
For this purpose we need <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption B.3 (Action-smooth proxy reward). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a> following two simple lemmas:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma B.6</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Flatness and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smoothness imply bounded gradient)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math> be differentiable and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smooth on a ball <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B(c,r)</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,
<math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|\leq\beta\|x-y\|\quad\forall x,y\in B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1.167em;" width="1.167em"></mspace><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|\leq\beta\|x-y\|\quad\forall x,y\in B(c,r)</annotation></semantics></math> .
Assume a "flat maximum" in <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, such that <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(c)-f(c+u)\leq\widehat{L}\quad\forall u:\|u\|\leq r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><mspace style="width:1.167em;" width="1.167em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c)-f(c+u)\leq\widehat{L}\quad\forall u:\|u\|\leq r</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then the gradient norm at c is bounded as</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(c)\|\leq\frac{\widehat{L}}{r}+\frac{\beta}{2}r\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(c)\|\leq\frac{\widehat{L}}{r}+\frac{\beta}{2}r\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">Based on the standard quadratic upper bound based on <math id="A2.SS1.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smoothness, we know</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="f(c+u)\leq f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{T}u+\frac{\beta}{2}\|u\|^{2}\quad\forall c+u\in B(c,r)\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>u</mi><msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>B</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c+u)\leq f(c)+\nabla f(c)^{T}u+\frac{\beta}{2}\|u\|^{2}\quad\forall c+u\in B(c,r)\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p9.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p9.2.1" class="ltx_text">We can rearrange this to</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="f(c)-f(c+u)\geq-\nabla f(c)^{T}u-\frac{\beta}{2}\|u\|^{2}\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">≥</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>u</mi><msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.0835em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c)-f(c+u)\geq-\nabla f(c)^{T}u-\frac{\beta}{2}\|u\|^{2}\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p9.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p9.3.1" class="ltx_text">By choosing the worst case <math id="A2.SS1.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u=-r\frac{\nabla f(c)}{\|\nabla f(c)\|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u=-r\frac{\nabla f(c)}{\|\nabla f(c)\|}</annotation></semantics></math> (if <math id="A2.SS1.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(c)\|=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(c)\|=0</annotation></semantics></math> the bound is trivially true), we have <math id="A2.SS1.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|u\|=r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|u\|=r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.p9.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="-\nabla f(c)^{T}u=r\|\nabla f(c)\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\nabla f(c)^{T}u=r\|\nabla f(c)\|</annotation></semantics></math>. Plugging this into the inequality and using <math id="A2.SS1.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(c)-f(c+u)\leq\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(c)-f(c+u)\leq\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> yields</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(c)\|\leq\frac{\widehat{L}}{r}+\frac{\beta}{2}r\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(c)\|\leq\frac{\widehat{L}}{r}+\frac{\beta}{2}r\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p9.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p9.4.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Note that robustness with radius <math id="A2.SS1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> implies robustness with any <math id="A2.SS1.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\prime}&lt;r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\prime}&lt;r</annotation></semantics></math> and we could further improve this bound by picking <math id="A2.SS1.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\prime}=\min(\sqrt{2\beta\hat{L}})\coloneq r^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≔</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\prime}=\min(\sqrt{2\beta\hat{L}})\coloneq r^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, if <math id="A2.SS1.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{*}\leq r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{*}\leq r</annotation></semantics></math>.
We do not do this here for ease of exposition.
We next need to connect the gradient bound of the expected <math id="A2.SS1.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{R}(s,a+Z)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{R}(s,a+Z)]</annotation></semantics></math> to a bound on the gradient of the pointwise <math id="A2.SS1.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{R}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{R}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma B.7</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Pointwise action-gradient is controlled by Gaussian-smoothing)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(a)=\widetilde{R}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(a)=\widetilde{R}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>. Under Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption B.3 (Action-smooth proxy reward). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a> and for <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>, define the Gaussian-smoothed reward</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{f}(c):=\mathbb{E}[f(c+Z)]\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{f}(c):=\mathbb{E}[f(c+Z)]\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla\bar{f}(c)=\mathbb{E}[\nabla f(c+Z)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla\bar{f}(c)=\mathbb{E}[\nabla f(c+Z)]</annotation></semantics></math> and for all <math id="A2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(c)\|\leq\|\nabla\bar{f}(c)\|+\beta\,\mathbb{E}\left[\|Z\|\right]\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(c)\|\leq\|\nabla\bar{f}(c)\|+\beta\,\mathbb{E}\left[\|Z\|\right]\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div id="A2.SS1.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS1.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.SS1.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smooth, it is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz gradient, and we can interchange gradient and expectation to obtain <math id="A2.SS1.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla\bar{f}(c)=\mathbb{E}[\nabla f(c+Z)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla\bar{f}(c)=\mathbb{E}[\nabla f(c+Z)]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, by Jensen’s inequality and <math id="A2.SS1.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smoothness,</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(c)-\nabla\bar{f}(c)\|=\Bigl\|\mathbb{E}[\nabla f(c)-\nabla f(c+Z)]\Bigr\|\leq\mathbb{E}\bigl[\|\nabla f(c)-\nabla f(c+Z)\|\bigr]\leq\beta\,\mathbb{E}\|Z\|\,," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em" stretchy="true">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em" stretchy="true">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(c)-\nabla\bar{f}(c)\|=\Bigl\|\mathbb{E}[\nabla f(c)-\nabla f(c+Z)]\Bigr\|\leq\mathbb{E}\bigl[\|\nabla f(c)-\nabla f(c+Z)\|\bigr]\leq\beta\,\mathbb{E}\|Z\|\,,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p11.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p11.2.1" class="ltx_text">then, by the triangle inequality and the previous line,</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">Then, we need to connect local smoothness and our knowledge of the gradient norm <math id="A2.SS1.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(c)\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(c)\|</annotation></semantics></math> at the center to violations of Lipschitz-continuity:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma B.8</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Pairwise robustness is bounded by local smoothness)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix a state <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>. Denote <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(a)=\widetilde{R}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(a)=\widetilde{R}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>. Assume that there exists a center <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in A</annotation></semantics></math> and radius <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smooth on the ball <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B(c,r):=\{a:\|a-c\|\leq r\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B(c,r):=\{a:\|a-c\|\leq r\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a,a_{1},a_{2}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{i.i.d.}}}{{\sim}}\pi(a|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mover><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mover><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a,a_{1},a_{2}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{i.i.d.}}}{{\sim}}\pi(a|s)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then for any <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|\leq\delta,|f(a_{1})-f(a_{2})|&gt;K)\leq 2P(\|a-c\|&gt;r)\,," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|\leq\delta,|f(a_{1})-f(a_{2})|&gt;K)\leq 2P(\|a-c\|&gt;r)\,,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
