<p id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for <math id="A2.Thmtheorem8.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\frac{1}{\beta}\left(\frac{K}{\delta}-\|\nabla f(x)\|\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>β</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>K</mi><mi>δ</mi></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\frac{1}{\beta}\left(\frac{K}{\delta}-\|\nabla f(x)\|\right)</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.5" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.p14" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p14.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p14.1.1" class="ltx_text">For any <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in B(c,r)</annotation></semantics></math>, by <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smoothness,</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla f(x)\|\leq\|\nabla f(c)\|+\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(c)\|\leq\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta\|x-c\|\leq\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta r\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla f(x)\|\leq\|\nabla f(c)\|+\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(c)\|\leq\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta\|x-c\|\leq\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta r\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p14.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p14.2.1" class="ltx_text">For any two points <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x,y\in B(c,r)</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="f(x)-f(y)=\int_{0}^{1}\nabla f(y+t(x-y))^{T}(x-y)dt\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><msubsup><mo>∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)-f(y)=\int_{0}^{1}\nabla f(y+t(x-y))^{T}(x-y)dt\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p14.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p14.3.1" class="ltx_text">taking the norm, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, and the bounded gradient, we get</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|f(x)-f(y)|\leq\int_{0}^{1}\|\nabla f(y+t(x-y))\|\|x-y\|dt\,\leq(\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta r)\|x-y\|\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">≤</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo </table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p14.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p14.4.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, if <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x,y\in B(c,r)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|\leq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|x-y\|\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, then</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|f(x)-f(y)|\leq(\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta r)\delta\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|f(x)-f(y)|\leq(\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta r)\delta\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A2.SS1.p14.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p14.5.1" class="ltx_text">Thus, the event <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|\leq\delta,|f(a_{1})-f(a_{2})|&gt;K\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|\leq\delta,|f(a_{1})-f(a_{2})|&gt;K\}</annotation></semantics></math> cannot occur when <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1},a_{2}\in B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1},a_{2}\in B(c,r)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta r)\delta&lt;K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\|\nabla f(c)\|+\beta r)\delta&lt;K</annotation></semantics></math>.
It thus can only occur if at least one of <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is not in <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B(c,r)</annotation></semantics></math>, which occurs with probability <math id="A2.SS1.p14.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(\|a-c\|&gt;r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(\|a-c\|&gt;r)</annotation></semantics></math>. By a union bound of the two events we get the result.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p15" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p15.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we can put it all together:</p>

<div id="A2.Thmtheorem9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.9</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(From <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>-<math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robustness to pairwise sharpness control)<span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assume a Gaussian policy with full row-rank Jacobian (Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption B.2 (Gaussian policy with fixed covariance and full row-rank Jacobian). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>), a <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>-smooth proxy reward <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{R}</annotation></semantics></math> (<a href="#A2.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption B.3 (Action-smooth proxy reward). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>), and fix a state <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math>-<math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> action robust, then for any <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K/\delta&gt;G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K/\delta&gt;G</annotation></semantics></math>,
we have gradient magnitude bound <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> and non-violating radius <math id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G:=\frac{\widehat{L}}{D}+\frac{\beta}{2}D+\beta\,\mathbb{E}\|Z\|\,,\quad r:=\frac{1}{\beta}\bigl(\frac{K}{\delta}-G\bigr)\,," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>D</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>β</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>K</mi><mi>δ</mi></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mi>G</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.170em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G:=\frac{\widehat{L}}{D}+\frac{\beta}{2}D+\beta\,\mathbb{E}\|Z\|\,,\quad r:=\frac{1}{\beta}\bigl(\frac{K}{\delta}-G\bigr)\,,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem9.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">such that</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.6" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS1.p16" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p16.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p16.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> and denote <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=\mu_{\phi^{*}}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=\mu_{\phi^{*}}(s)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Denote the PR as <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(a)=\widetilde{R}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(a)=\widetilde{R}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math>, mean action as <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=\mu_{\phi^{*}}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=\mu_{\phi^{*}}(s)</annotation></semantics></math>, and the smoothed proxy reward <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{f}(c)=\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)}[f(c+Z)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{f}(c)=\mathbb{E}_{Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)}[f(c+Z)]</annotation></semantics></math>.
By Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem2" title="Assumption B.2 (Gaussian policy with fixed covariance and full row-rank Jacobian). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a>, <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\sim\pi_{\phi^{*}}(a|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\sim\pi_{\phi^{*}}(a|s)</annotation></semantics></math> can be written as <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a=c+Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a=c+Z</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.
By Lemma <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem6" title="Lemma B.6 (Flatness and 𝛽-smoothness imply bounded gradient). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a> and, applied to <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{f}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>f</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{f}</annotation></semantics></math>, which we know fulfills Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem3" title="Assumption B.3 (Action-smooth proxy reward). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>, we obtain on <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B(c,D)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B(c,D)</annotation></semantics></math> the gradient bound</span></p>

stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\widetilde{R}(s,a_{1})-\widetilde{R}(s,a_{2})|&gt;K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mover encoding="application/x-tex">|\widetilde{R}(s,a_{1})-\widetilde{R}(s,a_{2})|&gt;K</annotation></semantics></math>, thus such violations can only occur if at least one action is outside <math id="A2.SS1.p16.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B(c,r)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo ∎</span></p>

</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>BT-Loss Lower Bound Based on Sharpness</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Now that we have connected <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D-\widehat{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>−</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>L</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D-\widehat{L}</annotation></semantics></math> robustness to the probability of actions pairs violating a flatness assumption <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(S_{K,\delta}|\pi_{\phi})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(S_{K,\delta}|\pi_{\phi})</annotation></semantics></math>, we now analyze the incurred excess BT loss <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{BT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>BT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{BT}}</annotation></semantics></math> due to these violations.
For this purpose, we make the assumption of a Lipschitz continuous true reward (Assumption <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem4" title="Assumption B.4 (Lipschitz-continuous true reward). ‣ B.1 Flatness in Parameter Space implies (𝛿,𝐾,𝜌)-pairwise robustness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>)</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition B.10</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For a prompt <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\sim P(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\sim P(s)</annotation></semantics></math>, a pair of actions <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a_{1},a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a_{1},a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>-Lipschitz true reward function <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, reward model <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, the excess-risk can be lower bounded as</span></p>
<table id="A2.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S_{K,\delta}:=\left\{(s,a_{1},a_{2}):\|a_{1}-a_{2}\|\leq\delta,|\widetilde{R}(s,a_{1})-\widetilde{R}(s,a_{2})|&gt;K\right\}" display="inline" action pairs for which the RM <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{R}</annotation></semantics></math> is not <math id="A2.Thmtheorem10.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" </div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\sim P(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\sim P(s)</annotation></semantics></math> denote prompts, <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\in\mathcal{A}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a\in\mathcal{A}</annotation></semantics></math> denote actions.
Let <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{*}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{*}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> be the true reward.
Under the BT model, the preference probability is <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p:=\Pr(Y=1\mid s,a_{1},a_{2})=\sigma(\Delta_{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p:=\Pr(Y=1\mid s,a_{1},a_{2})=\sigma(\Delta_{*})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{*}:=R^{*}(s,a_{1})-R^{*}(s,a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{*}:=R^{*}(s,a_{1})-R^{*}(s,a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>, with the logistic function <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma(x)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma(x)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-x}}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=1</annotation></semantics></math> means that <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is preferred over <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
A parametric reward model <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{R}(s,a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{R}(s,a)</annotation></semantics></math> induces the predicted pairwise probability <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q:=P_{\widetilde{R}}(Y=1|s,a_{1},a_{2})=\sigma(\Delta_{\theta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q:=P_{\widetilde{R}}(Y=1|s,a_{1},a_{2})=\sigma(\Delta_{\theta})</annotation></semantics></math>,<math id="A2.SS2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\theta}:=\widetilde{R}(s,a_{1})-\widetilde{R}(s,a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>R</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\theta}:=\widetilde{R}(s,a_{1})-\widetilde{R}(s,a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.
The BT loss in equation <a href="#S2.E3" title="Equation 3 ‣ Reward Models ‣ 2.2 Proxy Rewards ‣ 2 Background ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> can be rewritten as</p>

<p id="A2.SS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">but it can also be rewritten to explicitly consider a preference label <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>, where we have actions <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{1},a_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{1},a_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; then draw <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=\Pr(Y=1|s,a_{1},a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=\Pr(Y=1|s,a_{1},a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Taking expectations first over <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y|s,a_{1},a_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y|s,a_{1},a_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and then over <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s,a_{1},a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s,a_{1},a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math>, we get,</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{BT}}^{\pi^{1}}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{(s,a_{1},a_{2})}\mathbb{E}_{Y\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)}\left[\ell(q;Y)\right]\,," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>BT</mi><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.170em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{BT}}^{\pi^{1}}(\theta)=\mathbb{E}_{(s,a_{1},a_{2})}\mathbb{E}_{Y\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)}\left[\ell(q;Y)\right]\,,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.3" class="ltx_p">for <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell(q;Y)=-\left[Y\log q+(1-Y)\log(1-q)\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell(q;Y)=-\left[Y\log q+(1-Y)\log(1-q)\right]</annotation></semantics></math>. We proceed with this version.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lower Bound</h4>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Condition on <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s,a_{1},a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s,a_{1},a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> so that <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed. Then</p>

<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(p,q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(p,q)</annotation></semantics></math> is the cross-entropy and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(p)</annotation></semantics></math> is the entropy.
Averaging over <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s,a_{1},a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s,a_{1},a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and subtracting yields</p>

<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">For a fixed locality parameter <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and margin threshold <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the sharpness set</p>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Furthermore, we study the interval separation on <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{K,\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{K,\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>: On <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{K,\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{K,\delta}</annotation></semantics></math> we have <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{*}\leq L\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{*}\leq L\delta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\theta}\geq K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\theta}\geq K</annotation></semantics></math>.
By monotonicity and symmetry of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>

<tbody>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">If we assume <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K&gt;L\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K&gt;L\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, the minimum distance between these sets becomes:</p>

stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\inf_{p\in I_{*},q\in I_{\theta}}|p-q|=\min\left\{\sigma(K)-\sigma(L\delta),(1-\sigma(L\delta))-(1-\sigma(K))\right\}=\sigma(K)-\sigma(L\delta)\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(25)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Consequently, for every <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s,a_{1},a_{2})\in S_{K,\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s,a_{1},a_{2})\in S_{K,\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A2.E26" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.E26.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|p-q|\geq\sigma(K)-\sigma(L\delta)\,." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|p-q|\geq\sigma(K)-\sigma(L\delta)\,.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(26)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Since we can use the inequality <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p);\mathrm{Bernoulli}(q))\geq 2|p-q|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>KL</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p);\mathrm{Bernoulli}(q))\geq 2|p-q|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p,q\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p,q\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, combining with equation <a href="#A2.E26" title="Equation 26 ‣ Lower Bound ‣ B.2 BT-Loss Lower Bound Based on Sharpness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">26</span></a> yields:</p>

<div id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbf{1}_{S}:=\mathbf{1}\{Z\in S_{K,\delta}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{1}_{S}:=\mathbf{1}\{Z\in S_{K,\delta}\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicate membership of <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{K,\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{K,\delta}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We can make equation <a href="#A2.E27" title="Equation 27 ‣ Lower Bound ‣ B.2 BT-Loss Lower Bound Based on Sharpness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">27</span></a> valid for all <math id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(s,a_{1},a_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(s,a_{1},a_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> by multiplying the RHS with the indicator:</p>

<p id="A2.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">By taking the expectation of equation <a href="#A2.E28" title="Equation 28 ‣ Lower Bound ‣ B.2 BT-Loss Lower Bound Based on Sharpness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">28</span></a> and using equation <a href="#A2.E21" title="Equation 21 ‣ Lower Bound ‣ B.2 BT-Loss Lower Bound Based on Sharpness ‣ Appendix B Proof(s) ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>, we obtain the desired lower bound</p>

<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Connection of Gradient Regularization and Lipschitz Continuity</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For completeness, we reproduce the argument of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al. (2022)</a></cite>, which explicitly connects gradient regularization to Lipschitzness in parameters <math id="A2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">By the mean value theorem for differentiable <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, we have
<math id="A2.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="L(\theta_{1})-L(\theta_{2})=\nabla L(\zeta)^{T}(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\,," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>L</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ζ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L(\theta_{1})-L(\theta_{2})=\nabla L(\zeta)^{T}(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\,,</annotation></semantics></math>
with <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta=c\theta_{1}+(1-c)\theta_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ζ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta=c\theta_{1}+(1-c)\theta_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, with some <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality then yields
<math id="A2.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|L(\theta_{1})-L(\theta_{2})\|\leq\|\nabla L(\zeta)\|\|(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\|\,." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ζ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|L(\theta_{1})-L(\theta_{2})\|\leq\|\nabla L(\zeta)\|\|(\theta_{1}-\theta_{2})\|\,.</annotation></semantics></math>
Here, <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="||\nabla L(\zeta)||" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ζ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">||\nabla L(\zeta)||</annotation></semantics></math> takes the role of the Lipschitz constant and as <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{2}\to\theta_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{2}\to\theta_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="||\nabla L(\zeta)||" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ζ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">||\nabla L(\zeta)||</annotation></semantics></math> becomes <math id="A2.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="||\nabla L(\theta)||" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">||\nabla L(\theta)||</annotation></semantics></math>.
Thus we can see that gradient regularization leads to local Lipschitzness in parameter space, i.e., a flat local minimum.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<div id="lstnumberx25" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx25.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">optimizer</span>.<span id="lstnumberx25.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">step</span>()
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="A3.F9.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Implementation of finite-difference gradient regularization with GRPO in PyTorch</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In our experiments, we use the GR method <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karakida et al., 2023</a>)</cite> based on the finite difference estimate
<math id="A3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\phi}\|\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi)\|^{2}=\frac{\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi+\varepsilon\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi))-\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi)}{\varepsilon}\,." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mi>ε</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\phi}\|\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi)\|^{2}=\frac{\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi+\varepsilon\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi))-\nabla_{\phi}\mathcal{L}(\phi)}{\varepsilon}\,.</annotation></semantics></math>
We, thus, need to perturb the parameters <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math>.
Empirically, we found it to be beneficial to perturb only the parameters of the transformer blocks, including attention matrices, MLP weights and layer norm parameters, but not perturb the embedding layer or final output layer.
In principle, to calculate <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi+\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi))\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi+\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi))\|</annotation></semantics></math> we would also need to sample new actions <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}\sim\pi_{\phi+\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi)}(a|s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}\sim\pi_{\phi+\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi)}(a|s)</annotation></semantics></math> and estimate the gradient using these.
In practice, the computational overhead of this would be large, we reuse the same actions.
This introduces some bias which could be corrected use importance sampling, however, empirically we found this to be unnecessary.
We also need to choose a perturbation strength <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>.
While <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karakida et al. (2023)</a></cite> found a relatively large <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\approx 0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\approx 0.05</annotation></semantics></math> to perform best, initial experiments showed <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon=10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon=10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math> to perform well in our setting. We thus used it through-out our experiments.
We further use gradient clipping, both for the disturbance <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi)</annotation></semantics></math> and the gradient <math id="A3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi+\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi))\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mi>J</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi+\nabla_{\phi}J(\phi))\|</annotation></semantics></math>, each to 10.
We found this to prevent gradient spikes from destabilizing training.
The final combined gradient is then again clipped to 1.0 within DeepSpeed, as is done for the non GR methods as well.
We train our models using DeepSpeed ZeRO 2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Rajbhandari et al., 2020</a>)</cite> and use gradient accumulation.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For our RLHF experiments, we first need to train an SFT model, sample a training dataset <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\mathrm{RM}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>RM</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\mathrm{RM}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and train an RM.
For both, we use the code and hyper-parameters provided by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al. (2024)</a></cite>, which use the AdamW optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019</a>)</cite> with weight decay.
The SFT models are trained on the SFT dataset for one epoch.
For the summarization experiments, we use the SFT dataset provided by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, for Alpaca experiments we use the Alpaca-Instructions dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubois et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, but filter it by length following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ackermann et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
This length filtering to a maximum length of 512 tokens significantly decreases the computational cost.
Further, while Alpaca-Instructions contains separate splits for SFT, RM and RL training, we combine them to a single dataset as used in the summarization setting.
To obtain the RM training dataset, we sample pairs of responses from the SFT model and label them with either the Gold RM “Skywork-RewardLlama-3.1-8B-v0.2” <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite> for summarization or with GPT4.1-Nano for Alpaca experiments.
For the summarization tasks we use 278,496 preference pairs, for Alpaca Experiments we use 43,008 pairs for the 3B model and 86,016 pairs for the 0.5B and 1.5B models.
With the smaller data amount the 0.5B and 1.5B models did not produce sufficiently accurate RMs to use for subsequent GRPO updates.
We train the RMs, initialized from the SFT model, for one epoch on the dataset with the hyper-parameters as recommended by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Huang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
We then use the Dr.GRPO implementation provided by TRL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">von Werra et al., 2020</a>)</cite> with the hyper-parameters as listed in Table <a href="#A3.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ C.2 RLHF Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.
Additionally, we tuned the KL penalty strength <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> and GR strength <math id="A3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> as listed Tables <a href="#A3.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ C.2 RLHF Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and <a href="#A3.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ C.3 Gradient Regularization on Alpaca Farm ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Gradient Regularization Prevents Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback and Verifiable Rewards" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Gradient Regularization on Alpaca Farm</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We perform on the AlpacaFarm dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dubois et al., 2023</a>)</cite> with Qwen2.5 models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
Similar to the TL;DR experiments we first train an SFT model, sample pairs of responses from it, and obtain pairwise comparisons from GPT4.1 Nano.
We then train an RM based on these comparisons, initialized from the SFT model.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A3.T7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="A3.T7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">KL penalty values considered in hyperparameter optimization for Alpaca GPT4.1 Nano experiments.</span></figcaption>
<table id="A3.T7.5" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A3.T7.5.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A3.T7.5.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt">Experiment</th>
<th id="A3.T7.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Hyperparameters</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A3.T7.5.2" class="ltx_tr">
